validity.recommendation: Decide a single canonical representation: either keep P0477 as the whole-line network row OR the six segment rows P6697-P6702, but do NOT count both in any length/capacity aggregate. P0477 is the whole-line double of the segment set.
validity.researcher_notes: P0477 is a whole-line/network aggregate of the SAME physical pipe that is also entered as six separate operating segment rows in the roster (P6697 Dahshour->Giza 90km/36in; P6698 Al Kurimat->Beni Suef 30km/32in; P6699 Beni Suef->Minya 150km/32in; P6700 Abu qurqas->Asyut 147km/32in; P6701 Asyut->Sohag 121km/32in; P6702 Girga->Aswan 390km/30in). Those six lengths sum to 928 km == P0477's LengthKnown of 930 km, and their diameters read exactly 36,32,32,32,32,30 == P0477's Diameter string '36, 32, 32,32,32,30'. So P0477's Diameter field is literally the concatenated per-segment diameters and its length is the segment sum. GulfPub PE World Map independently represents the same line as six segments too (Dahsour->El-Koraimet 36in/56km; El-Koraimet->Beni Suef 32in/19km; Beni Suef->Abu Qurqus 32in/93km; Abu Qurqus->Asyut 32in/91km; Asyut->Gerga 32in/75km; Gerga->Aswan 30in/242km), operator Nile Valley Gas Company. The pipeline itself is unambiguously real and correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk (Mubarak inaugurated the Upper Egypt/South Valley line to Aswan Dec 2010; three independent trade/institutional sources below). The defect is purely the network-vs-segment double count across seven distinct ProjectIDs.

validity.recommendation: Treat Capacity=12 bcm/y as the 2014 design target, not commissioning-date throughput (8 bcm/y at 2010/11 inauguration); consider tagging as target. Re-check SegmentCost: sources give total investment LE 5.7 billion, not 9.3 billion.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity: petroleumafrica states 'With a current capacity of 8 bcm annually, capacity is expected to reach 12 bcm by 2014' - so GEM's Capacity=12 bcm/y is the 2014 target, corroborated but not the throughput at inauguration. (Oil & Gas Journal reported the still-partial South Valley network at ~166 MMcfd (~1.7 bcm/y) in 2007, i.e. an early-build figure, not a conflict with the completed-line design capacity.) SegmentCost: GEM records 9,300,000,000; petroleumafrica reports total investment across all phases of 'LE5.7 billion' - a material discrepancy (currency/scope unclear), so the 9.3bn figure is not independently supported. Length 930 km and diameters 30-36 in are corroborated (see fills). StartYear1=2009 sits mid-build: earlier phases were operating 2007-2008 (OGJ) but full commissioning to Aswan was late Nov / Dec 2010 (petroleumafrica), so 2009 is arguable and could be 2010.

validity.recommendation: Owner=Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co (EGAS) is defensible as ultimate owner, but the transmission operator is GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company); the Upper Egypt distribution operator is Nile Valley Gas Company. Consider recording GASCO as operator.
validity.researcher_notes: EIB names the promoter/operator of the Abu Qurqas-Asyut section as 'Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO), based in Cairo'. GulfPub attributes operation to Nile Valley Gas Company (the Upper Egypt gas distributor). petroleumafrica says construction was by several Egyptian government companies. GEM's Owner=Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co (EGAS) is the state holding parent and is acceptable as owner, but operator should read GASCO for the transmission trunk. Not an existence/classification problem - a role-precision caveat.

fills.researcher_notes: Dahshour->Aswan full line. petroleumafrica lists the stages (150 km Beni Suef->Abu Qurqas, 136 km Minya->Assiut, 100 km Assiut->Sohag, 408 km Sohag->Aswan, plus the Cairo/Dahshour->Beni Suef head) which sum to ~930 km; OGJ corroborates the northern phase lengths (150 km, 136 km). Matches the sum of segment rows P6697-P6702 (928 km).

Diameter range 30-36 in corroborated: petroleumafrica cites 30 in (Sohag->Aswan) and OGJ cites 32 in (northern phases); EIB/GulfPub also show 32-36 in on the head sections. The exact per-segment sequence '36,32,32,32,32,30' is the GEM/segment-row construction (matches P6697-P6702 diameters); the endpoint range is independently confirmed, the exact per-segment ordering is not, hence medium.

petroleumafrica: 'With a current capacity of 8 bcm annually, capacity is expected to reach 12 bcm by 2014.' So 12 bcm/y is the 2014 design target (8 bcm/y at 2010/11 inauguration). Single strong source for the 12 figure -> medium; recommend flagging as target capacity.

Line runs from the Dahshour offtake (Giza governorate, south of Cairo) down the Nile Valley to Aswan. petroleumafrica frames it Giza->Aswan; EIB places the mid section Abu Qurqas->Asyut. Dahshour is the recognized northern takeoff from the national grid.

EIB names GASCO as promoter/operator (not EGAS by name); GulfPub gives Nile Valley Gas Company as operator. No independent source explicitly names 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' as owner of this line. EGAS is the plausible state holding owner but is not verbatim-confirmed, so I leave Owner UNRESOLVED rather than attach a ref that does not name it. See attribution caveat: operator is GASCO.

GEM records 9,300,000,000 (currency/scope unlabeled). petroleumafrica states total investment across all phases reached 'LE5.7 billion'; EIB financed the Abu Qurqas-Asyut section at a total section cost of ~EUR 91 million. Neither supports 9.3 billion. Material discrepancy -> UNRESOLVED; do not attach a ref that contradicts the stated value.

StartYear1=2009 is not cleanly supported. Northern phases were operating 2007-2008 (OGJ; GulfPub segment start_years 2007-2008), while full commissioning to Aswan was late Nov / Dec 2010, inaugurated by Mubarak 30 Dec 2010 (petroleumafrica reports the Aswan inauguration event dated Jan 3, 2011). 2009 falls between; whole-line start is more defensibly 2010. Left UNRESOLVED pending a decision on network start-year convention.

routes.start_name: Dahshour offtake, Giza governorate (national grid takeoff)
routes.corridor_desc: Follows the Nile Valley south from the Dahshour grid offtake (south of Cairo, Giza governorate) through El Kureimat, Beni Suef, Minya/Abu Qurqas, Asyut, Sohag and Girga to Aswan - the same north-to-south Upper Egypt corridor described as five/six construction phases by petroleumafrica, EIB (Abu Qurqas-Asyut) and OGJ. Corridor identity is tight (named phase endpoints in independent sources); the exact pipe alignment is not published, but it hugs the cultivated Nile strip. Endpoint coordinates are the well-known city/locality centroids (EPSG:4326), not surveyed pipe coordinates.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints Dahshour and Aswan confirmed by independent sources; waypoints are the named phase-boundary towns (Beni Suef, Abu Qurqas/Minya, Asyut, Sohag, Girga) from petroleumafrica/OGJ/EIB. Coordinates are real place centroids from general geographic knowledge, not fabricated pipe surveys; no coordinate invented for an unnamed point. Route accuracy 'high' is consistent with the sourced corridor at network granularity.

summary: P0477 is real and correctly classed as a gas transmission trunk, but it is a whole-line double-count of segment rows P6697-P6702 (lengths sum 928km=930km, diameters=36,32,32,32,32,30); capacity 12bcm/y is the 2014 target not throughput, SegmentCost 9.3bn contradicts LE5.7bn, operator is GASCO not EGAS.
